newsitem.title: UK: Turkey tenders for 50-60kt low sulphur fuel in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Turkey tenders for 50-60kt low sulphur fuel in Dec.

text.p: Turkey's state oil company Tupras has tendered to buy 50-60,000 tonnes of one percent cracked sulphur fuel oil, trading sources said on Wednesday.
The material is to be delivered into Izmit and Izmir between December 25-30.
Bids must be received by December 9 and the award will be made two days later.
The company awarded a 25-30,000 tonne tender to an oil major earlier this week for low sulphur cracked material for delivery between December 15-17, but did not award its tender for M-100 product.

Fuel oil traders said the latest tender from Turpas will support an already tightish market which has seen prices nudge higher in recent weeks. Dealers say strong natural gas prices in the U.S. was prompting end-users there to opt to burn fuel oil -- hence limiting the amount of U.S. cargoes offered into Europe.
An earlier December cargo that was offered this week out of France is no longer available amid suggestions the material has gone inland.

Also giving a bullish tone is the continued strike at Elf's refineries in France. Now in its seventh day the dispute has already led to "increased buying interest" by traders worried about being left short.
